label: EU(7)-PIM: coxibs
title: Celecoxib or etoricoxib in an older person
statement: Celecoxib | In lists: 1, 2, 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Very high risk of GI bleeding, ulceration, or perforation, which may be fatal; cardiovascular contraindications | Dose adjustment/special considerations: The risk of bleeding may be reduced if combined with proton-pump inhibitors (use <8 weeks, low dose). E | Alternatives: Paracetamol; ibuprofen (≤3 x 400 mg/d or for a period shorter than one week); naproxen (≤2 x 250 mg/d or for a period shorter than one week). E Opioids with lower risk of delirium (e.g., tilidine/naloxone, morphine[d], oxycodone, buprenorphine, hydromorphone). E, P || Etoricoxib | In lists: 4 (A); 1, 2, 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Very high risk of GI bleeding, ulceration, or perforation, which may be fatal; cardiovascular contraindications | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Shortest possible duration of therapy. P Start with lower dose; the risk of bleeding may be reduced if combined with proton-pump inhibitors (use <8 weeks, low dose). E | Alternatives: Paracetamol; ibuprofen (≤3 x 400 mg/d or for a period shorter than one week); naproxen (≤2 x 250 mg/d or for a period shorter than one week). E Opioids with lower risk of delirium (e.g., tilidine/naloxone, morphine[d], oxycodone, buprenorphine, hydromorphone). E, P

plain_summary: Celecoxib and etoricoxib can cause serious stomach or bowel bleeding in older people. They can also cause cardiovascular harm. The person’s cardiovascular history, dose and duration of use matter.

medicine_groups.name: Celecoxib and etoricoxib (COX-2 inhibitors)
medicine_groups.note: Capsules and tablets count. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when celecoxib or etoricoxib (Group A) is supplied to a person aged 65 or older. One supply is enough. If the other criteria could be met and age is unknown, report only a possible finding and ask the pharmacist to confirm whether the person is 65 or older.
cannot_be_seen: Why the medicine was started, kidney function, blood pressure, heart disease and past stomach ulcers or bleeding. The history can show a recorded supply of stomach protection. It cannot show how long the pain medicine was taken, whether the person took the stomach protection, or whether they obtained it elsewhere or bought it without a recorded supply.
ask_the_gp: Whether the medicine is still needed, whether paracetamol or another lower-risk option would do, and the person's stomach and heart risk.
